question: What are the disadvantages to clipping negative PMI?

answer.free_form_answer: It may lead to poor rare word representations and word analogies.
evidence: Why incorporate -PMI? $\mathit {\texttt {+}PPMI}$ only falters on the RW and analogy tasks, and we hypothesize this is where $\mathit {\texttt {-}PMI}$ is useful: in the absence of positive information, negative information can be used to improve rare word representations and word analogies. Analogies are solved using nearest neighbor lookups in the vector space, and so accounting for negative cooccurrence effectively repels words with which no positive cooccurrence was observed. In future work, we will explore incorporating $\mathit {\texttt {-}PMI}$ only for rare words (where it is most needed).

title: Why So Down? The Role of Negative (and Positive) Pointwise Mutual Information in Distributional Semantics
answer_short: It loses information about negative cooccurrence, which contributes almost exclusively syntactic information and can be useful for rare words and analogies.
answer_rationale: Text 5 and Text 6 state that negative PMI (−PMI) contributes almost exclusively syntactic information and performs poorly on semantic tasks, except for syntax. Text 9 suggests that −PMI can be useful for rare words and analogies, where positive information is lacking. Clipping negative PMI at 0 (as in PPMI) thus discards this syntactic and rare-word-related information, which may be valuable in specific contexts.

question: Why are statistics from finite corpora unreliable?

extractive_spans: $\mathit {PMI}(w,c)$ goes to negative infinity when the word-context pair $(w,c)$ does not appear in the training corpus
evidence: Unfortunately, $\mathit {PMI}(w,c)$ goes to negative infinity when the word-context pair $(w,c)$ does not appear in the training corpus. Due to unreliable statistics, this happens very frequently in finite corpora. Many models work around this issue by clipping negative $\mathit {PMI}$ values at 0, a measure known as Positive $\mathit {PMI}$ ($\mathit {PPMI}$), which works very well in practice. An unanswered question is: “What is lost/gained by collapsing the negative $\mathit {PMI}$ spectrum to 0?”. Understanding which type of information is captured by $\mathit {\texttt {-}PMI}$ can help in tailoring models for optimal performance.
